question: Should OpenClaw adopt this requester identity, resolver ownership, and five-minute credential revalidation model as the permanent plugin SDK authorization contract for per-user MCP connections?
rationale: The patch is technically plausible, but tests cannot decide the acceptable revocation SLA, duplicate-registration policy, or permanent trusted-identity contract exposed to third-party plugins.

options.title: Harden and prove the contract
options.body: Require live two-requester isolation and revocation proof, define duplicate resolver ownership, and document the accepted revalidation SLA before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the current contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the five-minute revocation window and replacement registration semantics as the supported additive SDK behavior.

options.title: Pause the core API
options.body: Keep hosted per-user integrations on plugin-owned REST tools until maintainers approve a narrower or differently owned MCP extension seam.

recommendation.title: Harden and prove the contract
recommendation.body: Require live two-requester isolation and revocation proof, define duplicate resolver ownership, and document the accepted revalidation SLA before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns permanent plugin SDK architecture and a core credential-authorization boundary.
